evidence.observation: The criterion requires "a licence per source." In src/gnd/examples/literature/reference_set.py:105-109, labels.json receives one corpus-wide `licence` string, and its wording describes synthetic paraphrases without naming a licence. The source entries built at lines 67-69 have no licence field. tests/test_lr3_reference_set.py:56 checks only that the single string is nonempty.
The claimed evidence is "T1: licence note, counts 11/8/12 (A2), the corpus's files unchanged"; a licence note does not establish the required licence for each source.

concerns.recommendation: Record an actual licence for each of the twelve sources and check each entry in T1, or explicitly amend LR3-C1 and the close claim.
concerns.title: LR3-C1's per-source licence requirement is unproved

evidence.observation: LR3-C4 requires a scoring rule that distinguishes "found" from "found with the wrong predicate." In src/gnd/examples/literature/reference_set.py:90-103, anchored sections are indexed only by fact type and role values, without document ID; lines 145-169 then match by section and values without checking the gold fact's document. If two valid corpus documents assert the same fact, their labels receive both documents' sections, so one produced row can mark both gold facts found. tests/test_lr3_reference_set.py:115-140 has no repeated fact across documents.

concerns.recommendation: Include document ID in the anchor identity and require the attempt's section source to equal the gold fact's document; add a two-document repeated-fact case.
concerns.title: Repeated facts across documents can inflate recall

evidence.observation: The close reports "46 calls" for the recorded run. src/gnd/examples/literature/reference_fixture/README.md:55-56 additionally says "every byte of every document (7,708 bytes)" was read. The sections built in src/gnd/examples/literature/reference_set.py:74-78 and committed in roster.json total 7,662 bytes; 46 separator bytes lie between sections and are not shown to the producer. tests/test_lr3_reference_set.py:80 checks attempts, not bytes read.

concerns.recommendation: Say that all 46 sections were read under a 7,708-byte budget, and distinguish that budget from the 7,662 section bytes presented to the producer.
concerns.title: Reference README overstates bytes shown to the producer

response.summary: The recorded figures and replay path are supported, but one explicit criterion lacks its required metadata, and the scorer and documentation have narrower defects.
